text:
Sam: FYI — BrightCart (retail partner) wants to embed Redwood SDK into their POS terminals for a co-sell POC. Key asks: offline-first behavior, PCI compliance impact, certificate pinning, telemetry defaults (they want telemetry off), and how we charge per-transaction vs per-token. Can someone pick this up?
Nora: I can take the offline/arch piece. Short answer: SDK supports cache-first with configurable eviction and an async flush for telemetry. Important: we do NOT allow shipping model weights. For strictly air-gapped POS, we need Private on-prem contract.
Kellen: Pricing/monetization note — retail POS often prefers per-transaction pricing (predictable per-sale cost) or per-seat for kiosks. We can map per-transaction to token-estimates for typical receipt/summary flows. For POC propose a capped per-transaction rate + reserved node for background batching.
Priya: Security heads-up: PCI scope — if BrightCart sends raw PANs to our API that's not allowed. They must token-mask or redact PANs client-side before any outbound call. TLS1.3 mandatory, certificate pinning encouraged on POS firmware, mTLS for private connectors possible. We need their PCI assessor to confirm scope.
Sam: They specifically asked: "Can we do certificate pinning on the SDK and still rotate certs?" Also asked whether local HSM (on device) to store API keys is supported.
Nora: Certificate pinning supported; SDK exposes a pin-update hook so the app can rotate pins during maintenance windows. For API keys, we support hardware-backed key storage (PKCS#11) integration but need firmware docs. Recommend device stores a short-lived device token and we rotate backend credentials.
Kellen: Pricing sketch for POC: 30-day pilot with 500k transactions included, $0.10 per 1000 extra transactions (placeholder), plus 24/7 pilot support. Alternative: per-seat for registers + 1x Dedicated node to handle peak. I'll draft both scenarios.
Priya: On telemetry: default must be off for OEM POS builds. If they opt-in, telemetry must be aggregated (counts, latencies, error rates) with NO request payloads. Also need DPA + SOC2 cert before any telemetry collection.
Sam: BrightCart wants to keep all customer data in their network except anonymized metrics. They asked about a private connector or VPC peering. Which option is faster?
Nora: Private connector into their VPC is usually faster to set up for partners; peering requires network team coordination and can take longer. Either way, data stays in their network if we terminate inside their VPC. We'll need subnet/CIDR details.
Kellen: Another billing nuance: for per-transaction pricing we need an entitlement assertion from BrightCart on each call (e.g., X-Entitlement header) so we can reconcile usage to their commercial SKU. Recommend a signed JWT per device with exp window.
Priya: Compliance checklist items to request from BrightCart: 1) PCI SAQ type and assessor contact, 2) dataflow diagram for POS -> SDK -> connector, 3) device firmware HSM capabilities, 4) IdP metadata if they want SSO for admin portal, 5) SOC2 + DPA.
Sam: Action items: Nora — draft offline-first arch + cert pin rotation doc and sample SDK config. Kellen — provisional pricing (per-transaction vs per-seat + reserved node) and entitlement header design. Priya — security questionnaire + absolute blockers for PCI scope. I'll schedule a 30m kickoff with their engineering lead for Mon 8am PT.
billing-bot: Meeting created: "BrightCart POS embedded POC kickoff" — Mon 8:00 AM PT. Invite sent.
Nora: I'll post a sample config snippet before the call: ```json
{
  "endpoint": "https://private.brightcart.redwood.example",
  "auth_mode": "device_jwt",
  "cache": {"backend": "disk", "ttl_seconds": 7200},
  "telemetry": {"enabled": false},
  "cert_pinning": {"pins": ["sha256/AAAA..."], "auto_update_hook": true}
}
```
Kellen: I'll include an entitlement JWT example and provisional e2e cost table in the quote. Priya: please flag any absolute no-gos re: PCI before we share configs.
Priya: Absolute rule: never transmit PANs or full track data. If BrightCart insists on raw PANs for enrichment, that's a blocker unless they run our on-prem private package with separate contract.
Sam: Great — please drop drafts in #partnerships/brightcart and tag me. BrightCart asked for an anonymized sample transaction set (<=1000 rows) for a quick quality check if they mask PII.
